_what: Authored chip labels, keyed by node id. A 205px chip at 1.0x holds about 37 monospace characters; anything longer is middle-truncated by the renderer, which is a safety net rather than a design. Read by tools/build_l0.py and tools/build_l0_layout.mjs, both of which prefer an authored value and fall back to the derived one.
_why: Claude Design, 26 August 2026: "The chip label is an INDEX ENTRY, not a title. The test is 'can I tell which node this is', not 'can I read it'. The dossier carries the full string, always untruncated. The remaining work is content: author `short` per node at <= 37 characters." 46 of 110 overflowed and were being cut by an algorithm that cannot know which half matters -- it dropped the citation from 'Sec. 6802, James M. Inhofe NDAA for FY2023 (Pub. L. 117-263)', which is the half that identifies the statute.
_rules: NOTHING HERE ASSERTS A NEW FACT. Every value is a shortening of the label already on the record. No date, number, citation or name appears here that is not in the full label.
Drop the leading organisation where the band already says it; drop parenthetical glosses; keep the tail that distinguishes -- a volume number, a date, a section number.
An acronym is only used where it is the form the record itself uses (AAWSAP, AATIP, ODNI, AFOSI, NIDS, NASA). Never coin one.
Two nodes must never share a short. Volume I and Volume II, and the two Immaculate Constellation records, are the cases that force this.
_verified: 60 authored, every one 37 characters or fewer, no duplicates among themselves and no collision with the derived shorts already in use. Seven were added on 3 September 2026 for nodes the Danny Jones corpus build pushed over the L0 floor or over the 37-character chip; each is a shortening of the label already on the record and asserts nothing new. One was added on 18 September 2026 for arv-fluxliner, which the ARV corpus build created: 'Alien Reproduction Vehicle (ARV) / Flux Liner' is 45 characters, and ARV is the form the record itself uses throughout, so the short drops the parenthetical gloss and keeps both names the record carries.
